text:
sre-mira: heads up — apiserver latency + leader flapping in ap-southeast started ~06:05 UTC. seeing 500s from controllers and kubelet drain ops timing out. :warning:

sre-jordan: logs? kube-apiserver or etcd?

infra-omar: etcd follower reads spike and raft election churn. I/O queue depth on the local NVMe nodes jumped. hypothesis: noisy node causing WAL stall.

sre-mira: grabbing metrics — apiserver p99 token lat went from 40ms -> 2.3s; etcd quorum write latency up to 800ms. controller-manager Lease renewals are failing intermittently.

oncall-bot: Incident alert: control-plane-high-latency in ap-southeast-1 (priority: P2). Incident channel created.

eng-runtime-lee: also seeing outgoing egress retransmits between control-plane AZs for that region. network RTT variance high ~200-700ms. could be inter-AZ pathing.

sre-jules: past incidents where egress jitter + disk iops aligned with heavy scheduled GPU batch jobs launching in that region. any recent rollout?

infra-omar: yes — we had a Dedicated GPU scale-up earlier this morning (reserved-pool autoscale policy). many node attaches happening — kubelet/pod create storms. that increased control-plane fanout.

sre-jordan: that explains drain failures too. nodes trying to cordon/drain, but apiserver throttle + etcd latency cause pod deletion and finalizers to hang. GPU capacity ops are contending with control-plane ops.

sre-mira: quick mitigation idea: pause the Dedicated GPU pool autoscaler to stop further node attaches and backoff scheduled batch jobs. can infra do a soft throttle?

infra-omar: throttling autoscaler now (setting targetCount -> currentCount). also temporarily blocked scheduled cluster-autoscaler scale-up webhooks.

eng-runtime-lee: rolling restart proposal: restart controller-manager replicas one at a time to let leases re-acquire with less contention. should we also reduce controller syncs?

sre-jules: agree to single-replica restarts. but if etcd write latency persists, restarts will just churn. we should reduce write pressure on etcd: disable nonessential controllers (e.g., node-problem-detector syncs) and pause configmap-heavy cronjobs.

sre-mira: commands I'm running now: 
```
# check stuck finalizers
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.metadata.deletionTimestamp != null) | {ns: .metadata.namespace, name: .metadata.name, fin: .metadata.finalizers}'
```
found ~12 pods stuck in terminating across gpu-nodepools. most have volume detach finalizers.

infra-omar: I can offload etchost IO to standby storage: moving WAL to larger provisioned iops volume for the etcd leader in that zone. will take ~3-4m to reattach.

sre-jordan: if you do that, signal us before promotion. moving WAL will trigger leader re-elections. coordinate with controller restarts.

infra-omar: ack — starting snapshot + attach new iops volume now.

sre-mira: meanwhile I'm opening temporary routing rule to prefer intra-AZ control-plane traffic to avoid cross-AZ jitter (LB tweak). low-risk and reversible.

eng-runtime-lee: good. also recommend bumping etcd compaction interval and pausing heavy etcd watchers (metrics exporters) for the next 10m.

sre-jules: noted — pausing Helm operator reconcile loop (canary only) to reduce leader churn.

oncall-bot: Update: maintenance action in progress by infra-omar on etcd leader node. ETA 5m.

sre-mira: update 06:12 UTC: after LB tweak, apiserver lat p95 dropped from 1.6s -> 450ms. still seeing occasional lease lease renew errors but much fewer.

infra-omar: new iops volume attached and WAL moved. waiting for steady stats. I/O queue depth reduced ~70%.

sre-jordan: controller-manager restarts: restarting replica-2 now.

sre-jules: after restart, controller leases look stable. no new leader flips in last 90s.

sre-mira: confirming: kubelet drains that were failing are now progressing; 8/12 stuck pods moved to terminating -> deleted. remaining 4 are PV detach waits.

eng-runtime-lee: suggestion for follow-up: add a pre-scale control-plane pressure check to autoscaler so future GPU batch launches can be gated when control-plane p95 > X or etcd write latency > Y. avoids this tight coupling.

infra-omar: agree. also propose increasing provisioned iops on etcd volumes for gpu regions as a preventative measure (cost vs risk decision).

sre-jordan: cost note: increasing iops is ~+15% monthly for those regions. but reduces incident MTTR significantly for heavy attach/detach workloads. put on agenda for next infra weekly.

sre-mira: current status 06:18 UTC: control-plane stabilized, autoscaler still paused. will keep monitoring 30m then gradually resume GPU scale ops. great job all. :thumbsup:

noncall-bot: Incident resolved: control-plane-high-latency (duration: ~13m). follow-ups: PR for autoscaler gating, iops sizing proposal, runbook update for GPU-induced control-plane pressure.

sre-jules: filing the runbook updates and a post-incident note. tagging product for visibility on Dedicated GPU launch patterns.

sre-mira: thanks team. I'll leave the autoscaler paused until we have the gating PR merged.

sre-jordan: +1. closing thread unless anyone sees recurrence in next 10m.
